notes.title: -던
notes.text: -던 + noun looks back at something repeated or unfinished in the past: 내가 놀던 강 (the river I used to play in), 자던 중 (in the middle of sleeping), 할머니가 입던 옷 (clothes Grandma used to wear). It gives a sentence a gentle, nostalgic feel.

notes.title: -대요 / -래요
notes.text: In speech, -다고 해요 shrinks to -대요 and -(이)라고 해요 to -래요: 비가 온대요 (They say it'll rain), 이십팔 도래요 (They say it's 28 degrees). You'll hear them all the time in gossip and weather talk. 햇빛 = sunlight, 햇볕 = the sun's warmth, 햇살 = sunbeams.

notes.title: What's your 띠?
notes.text: Koreans often ask 무슨 띠예요? — "What's your zodiac animal?" — a polite way to work out someone's age. The twelve: 쥐 (rat), 소 (ox), 호랑이 (tiger), 토끼 (rabbit), 용 (dragon), 뱀 (snake), 말 (horse), 양 (sheep), 원숭이 (monkey), 닭 (rooster), 개 (dog), 돼지 (pig). A tiger and a bear star in Korea's founding myth.

notes.title: Season words
notes.text: 철 means "season" and attaches to other words: 여름철 (summertime), 겨울철 (wintertime), 제철 (in season — 제철 과일 = fruit in season). Spring is famous for 벚꽃 (cherry blossoms), 진달래 (azaleas) and 개나리 (forsythia); autumn for 단풍 (fall colors).

lessons.goal: Describe the night sky and the beach.

scene.ko: 해가 지고, 달이 떴어요. 바다 위에 달빛이 빛나요.
scene.en: The sun has set and the moon has risen. Moonlight shines on the sea.

scene.ko: 별이 정말 많아! 서울에서는 별이 잘 안 보이잖아.
scene.en: So many stars! You can hardly see stars in Seoul.

scene.ko: 저기 작은 섬도 보여. 섬에 빛이 하나 있어.
scene.en: I can see a little island over there too. There's a single light on it.

notes.title: The night sky
notes.text: 해가 지다 = the sun sets, 해가 뜨다 = the sun rises, 달이 뜨다 = the moon rises. 별 = star, 달빛 = moonlight, 빛 = light. Gangneung's 정동진 beach is famous for watching the sunrise (해돋이) over the East Sea.
